content.intro: This lesson introduces shell arrays and data handling as part of bash and shell fundamentals. Begin with an observation you can safely repeat, then explain what the result tells you and what it does not prove.
content.why_it_matters: Understand shell parsing, variable expansion, quoting, redirection, control flow, functions, and environment behavior.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Bash performs tokenization, expansions, redirections, and command execution in defined stages. Correct quoting preserves data and argument boundaries.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First, state what you expect from the example. Run it in the intended environment, capture standard output and any error message, and inspect the exit status where meaningful. Then connect the observation to this lesson: Shell Arrays and Data Handling. Do not infer more than the evidence supports.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake
content_blocks.text: A common mistake is to assume shell arrays and data handling behaves identically on every distribution, kernel, utility version, and administrative policy. Verify the installed tool and consult the matching manual before using the procedure elsewhere.

content_blocks.title: Safety and compatibility
content_blocks.text: Quote expansions to preserve intended values and argument boundaries. For commands that edit files, manage services, change network/firewall state, partition disks, change permissions recursively, or alter boot settings, use an isolated VM, take a snapshot/backup, review the exact target, and prepare a recovery path before acting.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the command is missing, check whether the required package is installed and which distribution you are using. If access is denied, do not immediately escalate to root; confirm the target path, identity, and required permission. If the result differs, capture the command, output, version, and environment so the issue can be reproduced.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember the core relationship: Bash performs tokenization, expansions, redirections, and command execution in defined stages. Correct quoting preserves data and argument boundaries. The goal is to explain the observed result, test a boundary case, and record a limitation rather than memorize a command in isolation.
